title: Oscillating current stimulation – slow oscillation stimulation during sleep
protocol: Recruit subjects with a normal sleep-wake cycle in the last 4 weeks.

Exclude individuals with seizure disorders, metallic foreign bodies, skull fractures, neurological diseases, severe systemic diseases affecting the central nervous system or cardiovascular regulation, or pregnant women.
Follow Ethical Principles for Medical Research Involving Human Subjects according to the Declaration of Helsinki.
Degrease and disinfect sites for stimulating electrodes (F3, F4, right and left mastoids).
Apply abrasive paste by rubbing skin with pressure on an area of about 1 cm².
Apply self-adhesive electrode paste to stimulating electrodes and stick them to the scalp.
Measure electrode impedance between each pair of stimulating electrodes (ipsilateral frontal and mastoid sites) must be < 2 kOhm.
Use a 2 kOhm resistor for each circuit to check that the applied current does not exceed the selected strength of 260 μA.
Set stimulator for slow oscillation stimulation: use currents oscillating at a frequency of 0.75 Hz (0.33 s-on/0.33 s-off with rising and falling slopes of 0.33 s).
Switch back to the correct settings immediately after checking current strength if different settings are used.
Plug the frontal electrodes cable into the anode (positive) sockets and the ipsilateral mastoids into the corresponding reference sockets for slow oscillation stimulation.
Check with documentation and/or manufacturer of the EEG amplifier that the stimulation current is uncritical for the amplifier.
After attaching the subject to the recording equipment and stimulation device, check that current is not felt by the subject when the stimulation is turned on for about 4 sec.
Monitor polysomnographic recording for eight consecutive 30-s epochs of sleep stage 2 or deeper NonREM sleep stage.
If the subject awakens or shifts into stage 1 sleep, wait for re-entry and maintenance of stage 2 sleep for eight consecutive 30-s epochs.
Set high pass filters at a sufficiently low frequency, e.g., 0.08 Hz, for recording slow oscillations.
Ensure a within-subject control by having an interval of at least 1 week between stimulation and sham stimulation sessions or two different types of stimulation sessions.
